As an application, these schemes are used to improve the accuracy in computing numerically the values of the scattering coefficients for an infinite-size lossless homogeneous isotropic slab, under dominant TM<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</sup> or TE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</sup> polarization.

articleTitle: Dynamically adaptive mesh refinement FDTD: A stable and efficient technique for time-domain simulations
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) technique [1] has been extensively employed in the modeling of microwave and optical structures, due to its simplicity and versatility. However, these FDTD qualities are partially compensated by the stability and numerical dispersion limitations on the choice of the cell size and the time step of the method, that render its application to complex and/or electrically large structures computationally expensive. In the past, a variety of static subgridding techniques [2]-[5] have been proposed, aimed at accelerating the conventional FDTD technique for structures with localized fine geometric features. According to such approaches, local mesh refinement is pursued in a priori defined regions of a computational domain, as dictated by physical considerations. For example, the presence of metallic edges, or high dielectric permittivity inclusions, would call for a locally dense mesh, embedded in a coarser global one. The use of local mesh refinement typically results in significant computational savings compared to the conventional FDTD, despite the fact that its implementation is associated with additional interpolation and extrapolation operations in both space and time.

articleTitle: Principles of time domain calculation of microwave resonator parameters
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The finite difference time domain (FDTD) method as well as the finite integration (FI) method is known as versatile simulation means for obtaining the electromagnetic field distribution or the response of the rf circuits. Considering that they work basically in the time domain, it should be a good practice to use their data without transforming to the frequency domain.

articleTitle: Inherent limitations in high frequency surface wave radar remote sensing based on Bragg scattering from Gaussian rough surfaces
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: An examination of the fluctuation in the Bragg spectral peaks in HF radar spectra of ocean backscatter is considered in the light of recent cross section models. It is well known that there are likely several factors giving rise to this phenomenon. Here we examine the effect which is caused purely in the context of a pulse Doppler radar being used to gather information from a time-varying random rough surface representable as a zero-mean, Gaussian random process. The finite width of the Bragg peak is presented as appearing naturally in the first-order cross section and the contribution to the power spectrum at each Doppler frequency point is seen to be affected by that at neighboring points.

articleTitle: Multiplex microwave holographic gratings: Sequential recording versus simultaneous recording
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Following the idea of multiplex optical holograms, multiple microwave holographic gratings are designed into one hologram, which can then be implemented by using the printed artificial dielectric technique. Two types of multiplexing methods are considered: sequential recording multiplexing and simultaneous recording multiplexing. Simulations for a four-beam recorded microwave hologram show the similarities and differences between the methods. It is found that the simultaneous recording method results in more diffraction waves, and is hence less efficient for the desired beam reconstruction than the sequential method. For beam splitting applications, both techniques can achieve the same results.

articleTitle: High-performance one-dimensional modal absorbing boundary conditions for FDTD modelling of waveguide structures
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is a popular time-domain numerical method for solving RF/microwave structure problems. It can compute the wideband electrical parameters such as S-parameters. In simulating a waveguide structure, effective absorbing boundary conditions are needed to terminate the waveguide while simulate the infinite long waveguide that create no reflections of modes. To address the issue, many absorbing schemes were proposed including the perfectly matched layer (PML) and one-dimensional modal absorbing techniques. However, they are derived analytically or semi-analytically, and therefore they present the errors or reflections that are not negligible, in particular, at or below cutoff frequencies. In this paper, we present our recent progress in developing high-performance absorbing boundary conditions for modeling waveguide structures: a one-dimensional modal FDTD method and a one-dimensional modal PML. They are derived directly from the FDTD formulation, and consequently they have numerical properties very close to the conventional FDTD method. When used as the absorbing boundary condition, they can achieve reflections of less than −200dB even at and below the cutoff frequencies. When used to obtain an incident wave in a waveguide, it can have the field solutions with difference of less than −200dB from those produced by the conventional FDTD method.

articleTitle: Dielectric resonator antennas for application in microwave tomography
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: This paper describes two prototype dielectric resonator antennas (DRA) designed to provide highly localized near field distributions, which are required in microwave tomography. Both antennas were designed and built for operation at an ISM frequency of 2.45 GHz. The first prototype is a dielectric cylindrical rod operating on the HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> guided mode and the second one is a more compact DRA consisting of a rod of rectangular cross section, partially metallized. This DRA operates on the rod's quasi-TEM mode and it has less severe fabrication tolerances. The measured near-field characteristics of both antennas are compared, and near-field images in the presence of a small scatterer simulating a tumor are presented.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable platform for software/hardware co-design of SDR base band pre-processing module
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: This paper proposes a reconfigurable platform for software/hardware co-design of base band pre-processing module of wideband wireless transceivers. The platform uses the Digital Signal Processors (DSP) and Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) to run advanced digital signal processing algorithms intended for the performance optimization of the transceiver radiofrequency front-end. Having the possibility to generate a variety of modulation techniques at high sampling rates and wide bandwidth up to 60MHz, the proposed platform is suitable for implementing innovative software defined radio transceivers' base band modules including digital pre-processing algorithms to boost the transceivers performances. An implementation and validation approach is also proposed. Taking advantage from the communication protocol between the DSP and the FPGA, the validation is done using the DSP it self for acquiring digital data at the output of each hardware function. A comparison of the emulation results to the high-level simulation ones is used to validate the hardware implementation and debug eventual bugs.

articleTitle: Fast time-domain indoor wireless channel modeling with a graphics processor accelerated S-MRTD technique
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Statistical models, often calibrated by measurements offer a straightforward way to characterize a wireless channel transfer function and associated effects such as signal fading and multi-path propagation [1]. On the other hand, site-specific models, estimate channel transfer functions taking into account the important effect of such parameters as material and geometric properties of the channel and potentially the types of antennas and propagation media involved. Ideally, the solution of Maxwell's equations in a given channel would accurately predict its properties, yet it typically requires extremely large computation times. On the other hand, simplified channel representations are fast yet inaccurate. Several efforts to address this inherent trade-off between speed and accuracy of wireless channel characterization have been reported in recent years. For example, techniques stemming from the hybridization of ray-tracing with the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) [2], pure FDTD approaches [3], finite-element (FEM) and fast-multipole (FMM) based methods [4], [5], have been applied to indoor propagation problems. The latter three techniques (FDTD, FEM, FMM) are aimed at the numerical solution of the full system of Maxwell's equations in the time or frequency domain. This paper pursues an alternative route to the time-domain modeling of wireless propagation problems, employing the scaling-function-based version of the MRTD technique, refereed to as S-MRTD [6]. In addition, the S-MRTD technique is further accelerated (by a factor of 30) through its implementation in a Graphics Processor Unit (GPU). Hence, an aggregate acceleration of two orders of magnitude over the conventional FDTD is achieved, rendering the proposed technique a real time tool for the analysis and design of indoor wireless channels.

articleTitle: 3D-butler matrix feeding networks for phased arrays
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The work described in this paper is being carried out within the framework of the NATALIA project (New Automotive Tracking Antenna for Low-cost Innovative Applications) funded by the ESA under contract number 18612/04/NL/US.

articleTitle: Modeling dielectric waveguiding structures with the method of lines
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: This paper discusses the method of lines and its application for generating the 2-D spatial distribution of vectorial mode fields supported by inhomogeneous waveguiding structures. Our formulation has been validated by comparing computed field distributions and mode wave impedances with analytic solutions and numerical results obtained from the literature when available. A complete analysis of an optical dielectric waveguiding structure is given along with an assessment of the accuracy of our technique.

articleTitle: A stripline fed printed wide slot antenna for UWB applications
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The Ultra Wide-Band (UWB) technology is now emerging. But the difficulty to design antennas having all the UWB features still restrains its deployment. Indeed, in the case of wireless multimedia communication systems, the antennas have to: be compact, low cost, easy to fabricate and integrate; they also have to be matched from 3.1 to 10.6 GHz, and to transmit very short pulses without distorting them. This last point implies that their radiation patterns are stable in the band and that their transient response is well-suited to UWB pulses. Among the proposed structures presenting interesting characteristics [1]-[5], the wide slot structure [1], [3] is a good candidate for UWB [3].

articleTitle: A low-profile conical helix antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The authors' papers [1][2] have revealed that a monofilar helix antenna radiates a circularly polarized wave. The diameter of this helix is increased from the bottom to the top. In contrast with this structure, this paper presents a monofilar helix whose diameter is decreased from the bottom to the top [3]. This antenna is called a conical helix antenna.

articleTitle: New bi-band fractal antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper Koch fractal antennas for bi-band operations at UHF frequencies (868MHz and 2.45GHz) are analyzed. In particular, two modified models of Koch fractal dipoles are compared to the standard bi-band Koch fractal dipole antenna. The goal is to reduce the size of the fractal antenna while still providing good gain and allow operation at multi-frequencies. A size reduction of 8% with respect to the standard Koch antenna is obtained, by using a new set of fractal antenna. The standard and the modified fractal Koch antennas are printed on glass-epoxy FR-4 substrate having a thickness of 1.6 mm and a relative permittivity of 4.4. The return loss parameter and radiation properties of the fabricated antennas are measured and compared with simulation results.

articleTitle: Review of DTV helix installation on unmanned airship
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: A number of telecommunications experiments were flown on an autonomous, 68 metre non-rigid airship in November 2004 [1]. Although the digital television broadcast experiment was successful, it was found that the signal was occasionally entirely lost when the airship passed directly over one receiving station. Initially, a quarter wavelength monopole on a simple model of the airship gondola was studied using a commercially available MOM software in attempt to identify features of the gondola that may have adversely affected the radiation pattern of the real broadcast antenna. The study was then extended to a more realistic conical beam, circularly polarised, quadfilar helix. The ground handling bars were found to affect the radiation patterns of both antennas.

articleTitle: A fully-electronic time-stretch system
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: We present an analog system capable of undistorted temporal magnification and compression of an arbitrary time-windowed electrical signal. The system is composed of three low-loss, high dispersion microstrip elements and an analog multiplier. Simulation results are presented demonstrating the 5X magnification of a 0.6 ns signal.

articleTitle: Performance of microstrip transmission line phase shifter with integrated ground plane membrane using low actuation voltage
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper, the simulation and measurement performance of a V-band microstrip transmission line phase shifter with ground plane integrated micromachined membrane is presented. The phase shifter fabrication technology and membrane deflection results are presented in another paper submitted in this symposium.

articleTitle: Efficient sensitivity analysis of lossy discontinuities using time-domain TLM
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: For the first time, the adjoint variable method (AVM) is applied to the efficient sensitivity analysis of lossy discontinuities with the time-domain transmission line modeling (TLM) method. Using only two simulations, of the original and adjoint systems, the sensitivities of the objective function with respect to all design parameters are estimated. The adjoint system is running backward in time, with its excitation extracted from the original simulation. The algorithm is illustrated through the wideband S-parameter sensitivity analysis of a dielectric resonator waveguide filter.

articleTitle: Single-band and dual-band multilayer transmitarray antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: A design procedure and experimental results are presented for single and dual-band, multilayer transmitarray antennas, operating at Ka-Tx/Rx bands (Tx=30 GHz, Rx=20 GHz). The performances of these transmitarray antennas are compared to reflectarray antennas of the same size. Efficiency figures of 50% and 35% were observed for single-band and dual-band transmitarrays, respectively, which were close to previously reported figures for reflectarray technology.

articleTitle: A high-gain planar array using parallel Yagi-Uda antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper the design of a high-gain planar antenna is presented. The antenna is designed to operate at 15GHz and has 24dB directivity. This design basically consists of four high-gain Yagi-Uda arrays, which are placed in parallel on a broad-side configuration and are excited uniformly through a feed network. The feed network and the antenna elements are all printed on the same substrate with the dimensions of 14cm × 20cm. The excitation is through a SMA connector with a 50ω coaxial cable. The 3dB beamwidth of the radiation pattern, in the E-plane, is 5 degrees while the H-plane beamwidth is 20 degrees. The system is impedance matched to 50ω at 15GHz.

articleTitle: A novel multi-frequency regularization method for the 2D inverse scattering problem under the born iterative method
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper, we consider the scalar transverse magnetic (TM), two-dimensional, time-harmonic, lossless inverse scattering problem. The goal of this problem is to determine an unknown permittivity contrast within some domain from field measurements taken outside that domain. It is well known that this problem is both non-linear and ill-posed in the classical sense, i.e., the solution is non-unique and small changes in the measured field data may cause arbitrarily large changes in the solution [1]. At a single frequency, the illposedness of the problem remains even under linearizing assumptions e.g., the Born approximation [2]. Under such an approximation, one obtains a Fredholm integral equation of the first kind and a discretization of the monochromatic integral equation yields an ill-conditioned system as a result of the illposedness of the underlying continuous problem [1]. The result of this ill-conditioning is that one must utilize some form of regularization, i.e., a method which selects a particular solution from within a class of possible solutions by imposing additional constraints.

articleTitle: A simple ionosphere model for correcting decimetre radio astronomical polarization measurements
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Polarization measurements using ground-based radio telescopes are susceptible to corruption by ionospheric Faraday rotation, which produces a shift in observed polarization angle that varies with time of day and with the ionizing solar flux. This effect can in principle be corrected using a ray-tracing approach along the path through the ionosphere in the direction of the celestial object under study, providing that values for the vector magnetic field and the scalar electron density are available for every point along the propagation path and for every time sample during the observation.

articleTitle: A 28GHz phase shifter using Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: A new phase shifter using Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) scheme combined with a post-based technique is presented. Phase shifting is achieved by changing the diameter and the position of inductive posts inserted in the SIW substrate. Simulations were carried out using one post, and two posts. Results have shown a good agreement with the theory. To prove the concept, prototypes have been fabricated for the two posts case. Preliminary experimental results show clearly that the use of inductive posts alter the phase of the wave traveling in the SIW waveguide.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic fields due to illuminated subsurface conductors: A ground penetrating radar application
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: A new approach based on a ground penetrating radar is proposed to detect and locate a metallic object hidden in a lossy ground. In this approach, the object is illuminated by a dipole antenna and the resultant scattered electric field is monitored at a distance above the ground. The detection and locating of the object are based on the simulation results obtained using a full-wave solution of the forward-scattering problem with the least simplifying approximations. To solve the problem, the metallic object is first modeled as a network of thin-wire conductors. The governing electric field integral equation (EFIE) is then solved efficiently using the method of moments in the frequency domain. Also, the air-ground interface is modeled using the modified image theory.

articleTitle: Design of very thin wide band absorbers using particle swarm optimization
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper design of very thin and broadband electromagnetic absorbers is described. For normal incidence a five-layer absorber with 7.6 mm thickness with reflection coefficient below 20 dB over the frequency range 0.1 < f (GHz) < 10 has been achieved. Genetic Algorithms (GA) and three variants of particle swarm optimization (PSO) are applied to this problem. In order to show the capabilities of PSO algorithm in absorber design three different absorber designs are optimized. To alleviate local minima problem, a modified lbest PSO (MLPSO) is employed. Simulation results show that MLPSO searches the space faster and more efficiently, proposing it as a strong tool for designing electromagnetic absorbers.

articleTitle: Mode matching and point matching techniques for dispersion curves of microstrip line structures
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper the mode matching (MM) technique is utilized to find the dispersion curve of a regular microstrip line. To convert the algebraic equations to a matrix form, a method is invoked which is similar to the well-known point matching (PM) technique. The results of this hybrid technique (MM-PM) are in close agreement with those from published work.

articleTitle: Design of high-Q micromachined tunable capacitors for RF applications
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Two high-Q micromachined electro-mechanically tunable capacitors are presented. The proposed designs are CMOS-compatible that can be integrated with CMOS circuit in a single die. In these structures there is no need for cantilever beams which introduce considerable series resistance to the capacitor and decrease the quality factor. So our proposed structures achieve better Q in a smaller area. The simulated 1pF full plate capacitor with aluminium deposition on top plate shows a tuning range of 42% and a Q of 47 at 1 GHz. For the comb structure the tuning range is 43% and Q is 45 at 1 GHz. Pull-in voltage is 3.5 V for both capacitors. The S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> responses are reported for a frequency range from 1 up to 4 GHz.

articleTitle: Indoor wireless reception improvement using cross-polarized multipath signals
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Previous work has noted the distinct characteristics of vertically and horizontally polarized multipath components for indoor non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environments. Using measured data, the receiver signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) for coherent and noncoherent combining of the co- and cross-polarized multipath components are compared to those obtained with omnidirectional reception for vertical or horizontal polarizations. It is seen that significant improvements in SNR can be achieved using intelligent combining with polarization diversity. Furthermore, it is observed that when the receiver is unable to resolve multipath components, coherent combination of both orthogonally polarized signals components provides a consistent advantage over vertically or horizontally polarized omnidirectional reception. At higher bandwidths, the increased resolution improves the performance of all techniques however the dual polarization multipath combining retains its relative advantage over the other techniques.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the FVTD technique for electromagnetic field problems containing highly inhomogeneous structures
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper, the cut-off frequency of the dominant mode of a finned waveguide is computed using the Symmetric Condensed Node Transmission Line Matrix (SCN-TLM) and Finite Volume Time Domain (FVTD) methods. The cut-off frequencies are computed for various sizes of fins as well as fine and coarse meshes. The values of the cut-off frequencies are obtained and compared with each other and with a benchmark solution.

articleTitle: Ultra wideband shaped cylinderical dielectric resonator antenna for commercial wireless bands
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Over the past years, dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) technology has received extensive attention. This is in view of some attractive features, which include no conductor loss, light weight and high radiation efficiency [1]. Some of the recent work focuses on enhancing the impedance bandwidth of a DRA by introducing parasitic elements, cascading resonators or shaping the DRA elements [2-9].

articleTitle: One dimensional clustered dielectric particle (CDP) parallel-plate waveguide (PPWG) structure
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Recently, metamaterials (MTMs) [1] have drawn considerable attention in the engineering and physics communities. Most of the MTMs reported to date are constituted of metallic inclusions periodically arranged in a host dielectric medium. Due to the presence of metal, which exhibits prohibitive losses at high frequencies, these MTMs are practically restricted to a frequency band below 100 GHz. In addition, metal-made structures, even at the low-end of the microwave range, are prone to short-circuiting and parasitic coupling with circuitry when used as a substrate in planar technologies. Therefore, purely dielectric MTM structures are strongly needed, to provide both optical MTMs and efficient microwave materials.

articleTitle: Transverse electric wave scattering by elleptic chiral cylinder
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: An exact boundary value solution for the scattering of transverse electric (TE) wave by an elliptic chiral cylinder is developed and presented in this paper. The solution is based on the separation of variable technique in the elliptic cylinder coordinates system and expressed in terms of Mathieu and modified Mathieu functions. The incident, transmitted and scattered electromagnetic waves are expressed in terms of infinite series of wave functions. The matrix form of the expansion coefficients is found by applying the boundary conditions and orthogonality of the Mathieu functions. Numerical results of the bistatic and monostatic (back-scattered) echo widths for co- and cross-polarized waves, for various cases are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: The effect of air gap on the radiation performance of microstrip-slot coupled rectangular dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: A Microstrip-Slot Coupled Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna (RDRA) operated at the dominant TE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</inf> mode of operation is investigated numerically and experimentally. The effect of air gap between feeding slot and the resonator on the radiation performance of the RDRA is studied A few experimental set-ups were also examined and the antenna parameters were measured. It is shown that there is a good agreement between simulated results and those obtained by experiments.

articleTitle: Application of the Flexible Local Approximation Method to photonic crystal cavities
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a recently developed numerical technique, the Flexible Local Approximation Method (FLAME), to compute the resonance of two dimensional (2-D) photonic crystal (PC) cavities, formed by a defect in a regular array of dielectric rods. FLAME is finite-difference-like method which is ideally suited to problems consisting of large numbers of identical structures. The anisotropic perfectly matched layer (PML) is used as an artificial absorbing layer to truncate the computational domain. FLAME and PML boundaries are applied to PC cavities with 3×3, 5×5, and 7×7 arrays of rods.

articleTitle: Hexagonal Fresnel zone plate antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: A novel hexagonal Fresnel zone plate antenna is introduced and compared to the traditional circular Fresnel zone plate antenna. The comparison was carried out in simulation by using a finite-difference time-domain software. Although the circular lens performs better, the hexagonal geometry is better suited for arrays and provides the ability to both improve the sidelobe level and shift the sidelobe location away from boresight. This is accomplished by appropriately rotating the rings that make up the lens and is achieved without sacrificing directivity or 3dB beamwidth.

articleTitle: Perfectly matched plane wave generated by a time domain multipoint 1D propagator for total field/scattered-field finite difference time domain (FDTD) formulations
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Solutions to improve the Total Field Scattered Field formulation (TF/SF) in FDTD developed by Taflove in the 70s have been attempted by many researchers [1,2,3]. When coupling between 1D-auxiliary grid Yee update equation to 2D or 3D, the time domain method suffers inaccuracies due to numerical mismatch. Using linear time-invariant system transfer functions, Schneider et al. proposed a frequency domain solution which eliminates the need for the traditional 1D-auxiliary grid and in principle can produce a perfect incident plane wave at the Huygen's surface [2].

articleTitle: A geometric property of the functional associated with general systems of algebraic equations
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: A functional is associated to general systems of linear algebraic equations such that, for any point defined by an arbitrary set of unknowns, the position along its gradient which is the nearest to the system solution point can be determined directly from the value of the functional and of the gradient. Remarkably, the distance along the gradient to the point closest to the solution point is equal to the ratio of the value of the functional to the magnitude of its gradient at the starting point. By means of simple matrix transformations, this property can be employed to construct independent equations satisfied only by a part of the original system unknowns.

articleTitle: An innovative spiral scanning over an oblate ellipsoid for NF-FF transformation
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The techniques for reconstructing antenna radiation patterns from near-field (NF) measurements have been widely investigated in the last decades and used for applications ranging from cellular phone antennas to large phased arrays and complex multi-beam communication satellite antennas. They have been proved to be an efficient and attractive alternative to conventional far-field (FF) range and compact range measurements. Moreover, NF measurements may be performed in a controlled environment, as an indoor shielded anechoic chamber, thus eliminating problems due to weather conditions (rain, snow, etc.), electromagnetic interferences, and other.

articleTitle: Large antenna measurement in fresnel region using direct far-field measurement system
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The reflector for the satellite communications or the array antenna with a few hundred radiating elements has the huge aperture dimension, and its far-field range satisfying D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">far</inf> = 2L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/λ is usually out of the its own anechoic chamber, where, L is the aperture diameter, and λ is free-space wavelength. For example, the far-field distance of the antenna of L=20 λ operating at 10 GHz is 24 m. Some antennas cannot be measured in Anechoic chamber because its far-field distance is a few km.

articleTitle: The signal processing system for the DRAO phased array demonstrator: PHAD
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Sampling the fields near the focal plane of a paraboloid, with an array of feeds, has numerous advantages. With appropriate signal processing, multiple-beams can be formed yielding a broader field of view compared to a conventional single-element feed [1-7]. Additionally, these beams can be shaped and optimized, for instance to maximize gain or minimize spillover [4,8]. As well, corrections can be applied permitting certain system imperfections, such as coma, to be compensated [9-12].

articleTitle: Simulation studies of the continuum structure in ionospheric Stimulated Electromagnetic Emission
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Stimulated Electromagnetic Emission (SEE) is thought to be produced during ionospheric heating experiments as a result of parametric decay instability processes. This phenomenon is mainly attributed to plasma turbulence excited by high frequency (HF) heater in the altitude region where the pump frequency ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is near the upper hybrid frequency ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">uh</inf>. In this paper, parametric instability processes are studied using 1-D electrostatic Particle-in-Cell (PIC) simulation models. The plasma is driven with a uniform oscillating electric field directed nearly perpendicular to the background magnetic field B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, this is to consider interactions near the plasma upper hybrid frequency ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">uh</inf>. The pump frequency is varied to consider the effects on the simulation electric field power spectrum. This study will mainly focus on studying the development of the broad downshifted sideband, the Continuum structure, attributed to parametric decay instability. The relationship between the simulation results and the experimental spectrum data for the Continuum feature is also discussed in this study.

articleTitle: Phase properties of a variable-patch-size microstrip reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In general, despite the seemingly many advantages of the microstrip reflectarrays, one of the most serious shortcomings of these devices is the issue of limited bandwidth [1]. To improve the bandwidth of the variable-patch-size microstrip refiectarray, the variation in the patch size must be studied more thoroughly so that its phase variation properties, and thus its bandwidth characteristics, can be determined more accurately. Other important parameters such as the substrate relative permittivity and the substrate thickness are analyzed as well.

articleTitle: Performance of finite rectangular microstrip antennas with finite conductor and dielectric back planes at 1.8 Ghz
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The performance of finite rectangular microstrip antennas with finite substrate and ground planes, finite ground planes, finite substrate, and finite conductor and dielectric back planes is studied. The effects of back plane extension beyond the patch radiating edge and in the lateral direction are shown. HFSS and ENSEMBLE have been utilized for the analysis.

articleTitle: Aperture oriented approach to the analysis of artificial magnetic conductors and first-order circuit model validation
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: A MoM analysis procedure for Artificial Magnetic Conductors, using equivalent magnetic currents is presented, and its advantages discussed for both patch-type and aperture-type AMC.A quite accurate equivalent circuit has been extracted from our MoM results, using a curve-fitting procedure.

articleTitle: Reflection and transmission by thick wires in reinforced concrete
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper, the reflection and transmission properties of reinforced concrete are investigated by using a two-dimensional (2D) Method of Moments/Green's function (MoM/GF) model for an array of parallel circular cylinders inside a lossy dielectric slab. In doing so, a thin wire grid is used to model each thick circular cylinder subject to the “same surface area” rule of thumb. As a result, this model helps enhance the accuracy of reflected and transmitted fields by means of wire grid modeling.

articleTitle: Optimization of dielectric fresnel lens thickness for maximizing gain
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The effects of the thickness and dielectric constant of a phase-correcting Fresnel lens on the mismatch loss and shadow blockage with the goal of improving the overall antenna gain are investigated. Fresnel lenses designed with three different focal length-to-diameter (F/D) ratios, three different dielectric constants, and two different phase corrections, are examined for a total of 18 cases. For each case, the gain is determined as a function of lens thickness. Significant variations in gain are observed, making the lens thickness an important parameter in the design of phase-correcting Fresnel lenses.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling of DRA's in staggered configuration
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Mutual coupling of rectangular DRA in staggered configuration is investigated. Two staggered arrangement is studied, one rectangular staggered DRA and the other circular staggered DRA. The FDTD method with a UPML boundary condition is used for simulations.

articleTitle: New microstrip miniaturized loop filters for a mobile communication system
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper we present a procedure for designing microwave bandpass filters with a single pair of attenuation poles at finite frequencies. The filter topology consists of pentagonal open-loop resonators where the couplings between nonadjacent resonators are responsible for the attenuation poles at finite frequencies. The coupling coefficients between the open-loop resonators are determined using the circuit elements of the low-pass prototype. A fourth order filter with a fractional bandwidth of 10% at 1.8 GHz is designed and fabricated. The experimental results are presented and commented.

articleTitle: Design of highly sensitive H-field probes for near-field EMC & HAC assessment
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a sensitive miniaturized H-field probe for accurate magnetic near-field measurements in the gigahertz range. The probe performance was verified by measuring near-field electromagnetic field distributions above a half-wave dipole antenna operating at 1.85GHz. Very high sensitivity was obtained from the developed probes. Sensitivity of this probe was found to be better than traditional dosimetric E-field probes. High-sensitivity probes are useful in EMC/EMI assessments.

articleTitle: Comparing antenna and beam selection for different selection strategies over measured indoor MIMO-OFDM channels at 6 GHz
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Selection of a subset of receiver antennas for a multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) wireless link has been studied by many as a way to reduce cost and complexity in a spatial multiplexing MIMO system, while providing diversity gain. However, most of these studies have been over simulated channels. In this paper, we use measured indoor channels. We compare three selection criteria to be implemented at the access point in an indoor wireless LAN: minimum symbol error rate (SER), maximum capacity, and the maximum of the minimum singular value of the MIMO channel. The comparison is based on SER which is computed for 802.11a OFDM waveforms, where the same selection is made for every subcarrier. The dual-user scenario is considered, and the access point comprises two RF beamformers that are separated by at least 5 m, such that the beam selection is done jointly for the two beamformers.

articleTitle: Cavity resonators
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper, properties of few different types of cavity resonators are investigated using commercial full wave softwares. The simulations are performed using Ansoft HFSS (FEM) and Microstripes (TLM). A new tunable coaxial cavity with dual resonators is designed and fabricated. A parametric study of helical resonators is presented along with resonant properties.

articleTitle: A dual-polarized CPW-FED patch antenna for wireless applications at 2.45 Ghz
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: This paper presents the design and the fabrication of a dual-polarized patch antenna fed by two coplanar waveguides (CPW) for operation around a center frequency of 2.45 GHz. In order to achieve an inductive coupling with the radiating patch, each CPW line is ended with a perpendicular slot of λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>/4 in length, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> is the wavelength on the substrate. Results show that an impedance bandwidth of 40MHz (1.63%) is obtained using a single layer of substrate. The simulated return loss for both polarizations is less than −40 dB and isolation between ports is better than −22 dB. For validation purposes, a prototype of the antenna and experimental results are also presented.

articleTitle: Tunable microwave transmission in a periodically corrugated waveguide
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The main physical phenomenon caused by periodicity is Bragg reflection. It results in the opening of the forbidden gap in the spectrum of the periodic structure. The Bragg reflection occurs both in the case of unbounded periodic medium as well as in a case of a bounded periodic structure like a periodic waveguide. However, in the waveguide geometry dispersions become more complex due to their folding and crossing. As a result, besides Bragg reflections there arise non-Bragg reflections in the periodic waveguide. The spectrum of a planar waveguide acquires qualitatively new, and very promising from practical point of view, features if the periodicity is introduced into the waveguide by the lateral modulation. In the latter case the transmission properties become controllable due to opportunity to change the lateral modulation profile. For example, gaps can be tuned by means of shifting of periodic boundaries [1-3].

articleTitle: Superluminal group velocity in CRLH transmission line metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Since the pioneering works of Brillouin and Sommerfeld [1], the intriguing concept of group velocity has generated a lot of academic excitement. In particular, many papers, both theoretical and experimental, have reported superluminal group velocity and have explained this phenomenon in the context of Einstein's relativity [2]-[7]. In general in these papers, superluminal group velocity is associated with anomalous dispersion (∂n / ∂ω < 0) and occurs in a strongly absorptive band (stop-band) of the propagation medium, where extremely little transmission is achieved. In fact, such superluminal transmission occurs in many engineering devices, such as in microwave filters, but has then little practical interest because both of high distortion (due to high dispersion) and low transmission (due to stop-band). As pointed out by Brillouin and Sommerfeld, the group velocity under these conditions do not have a real physical meaning, since no information can be transmitted (the input pulse so much distorted that its detection at the output is impossible.) and should rather be replaced by the more meaningful concepts of energy velocity or front velocity.

articleTitle: The DSP implementation of the LINC amplifier to improve ACPR and imbalance performance
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: This paper is projected towards improving the adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR) for LInear amplification using Nonlinear Component (LINC) power amplifiers in OFDM based wireless systems using digital baseband filtering for branch signals. The IEEE802.11g standard, which operates at 2.4 GHz, is used to show the amount of improvement. Results show that the ACPR is improved using a least square filter, from −26.1dBc to −63.8dBc, without deteriorating the overall system power efficiency.

articleTitle: THz probe for investigation of cells trapped by a BioMEMS
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: We have demonstrated recently an original planar excitation of surface wave on a single wire transmission line. This propagation mode is well suited for the living cell investigation because we deal with a micrometer spatial resolution. We combine in a BioMEMS, microfluidic circuits and THz propagation around a wire taken as a microscopic antenna.

articleTitle: A novel performance-prediction model of subharmonic self-oscillating mixers
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper, a novel model for accurately evaluating the performance behaviour of subharmonic self-oscillating mixers (SOM) is presented. This model permits to investigate on the effects of various design parameters of SOMs namely in terms of conversion gain, IF frequency, noise figure, and intermodulation distortion. Such an accurate model is specifically important in the design of millimeter-wave circuits due to their high fabrication costs.

articleTitle: MIMO channel model for different antenna elements and arrays
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: An accurate knowledge of a communication channel is extremely important in designing radio systems since the performance of a receiver is highly dependent on the ability of predicting the wireless communication channel. Therefore, channel modeling has become a subject of intense research, nowadays [1], [2].

articleTitle: Adaptive microwave beamforming using fast perturbation
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: MICROWAVE beamforming (MBF) is advantageous over digital beamforming (DBF) in several regards [1]. First, due to a lower number of RF down-converters and analog to digital converters (ADC), MBF structures have lower size, weight and battery power consumption. Second, due to weighting and combining of signals in the analog domain and avoiding quantization errors, MBFs have higher dynamic and suppression range. However, a problem with any MBF is the lack of antenna elements' signals in the processor which prohibits using existing DBF algorithms directly. Different perturbation techniques have been proposed to carry out adaptive beamforming using MBF structures [2]-[6]. In [7], [8] adaptive algorithms have been presented for MBF structures with phase shifters alone. In [9]-[12] perturbation techniques have been presented for microwave aerial beamforming. The main limitation in all these techniques is the long perturbation time.

articleTitle: Identification of a cylindrical target using RCS measurements made along a radar trajectory
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: This paper concerns the identification of a cylindrical target as seen by a radar traveling on a trajectory. It describes a procedure for determining the dimensions and aspect angle of the cylindrical target using radar cross section (RCS) measurements made along the radar trajectory. A comparison between the RCS measurements and the computed RCS is shown and the dimensions and the aspect angle of the unknown cylindrical target are deduced.

articleTitle: UTD asymptotic code used for antenna implementation on electrically large structures
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The implementation of antennas in a complex environment still remains a problem when high frequencies are considered [3]. The Uniform geometrical Theory of Diffraction (UTD) is one of the most convenient techniques to solve this problem [1,2]. This method is applied in the software IDRA developed at IEEA.

articleTitle: Determination of global phase center of multimode circular microstrip antenna with minimizing crosspolarization
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Microstrip antennas have been receiving widespread attention in communication systems due to their attractive features like light weight, low cost, capability of integrating with active circuits and so on [1]. They can also be good candidates as reflector antenna feeds, by optimizing their radiation characteristics [2]. In this particular application, it is important to know their phase center location and minimize the crosspolarization. For rectangular microstrip antennas radiating the fundamental mode, the effective point of operation is generally well defined and has been investigated in [3].

articleTitle: Control of radar reflections with metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Flat metallic plates, dihedrals and trihedrals often cause undesirable specular radar reflections. These reflections can be reduced by applying a radar absorbing material on the metallic surfaces. The radar cross section of a target be thus modified. Another approach to alter a radar reflection from a target would be to cover the target with a material that would change the reflection from specular to non-specular. The concept is depicted in Figure 1.

articleTitle: Software defined six-port receiver for OFDM modulation
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) has been identified as a potential method to enhance the performance of wireless communication links degraded by cosite interference, impulsive noise and frequency selective fading. In this paper, an OFDM software defined radio (SDR) receiver based on a wideband substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) six-port circuit is described and analyzed. A six-port direct receive for OFDM modulation is proposed for the first time. The proposed receiver provides a simple means to obtain a low cost module for OFDM modulation. Simulated results of noise performance of the SDR six-port based receiver are shown and discussed. The combination of OFDM and SDR technology provides great system flexibility, significant reduction of system development cost and very high potential for software reuse.

articleTitle: Development of frequency domain channel simulator for broadband wireless access systems using channel measuremens
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: All Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing OFDM, simulators that have been built so far employ a finite impulse response (FIR) tapped delay line filter. A channel simulator for OFDM can also be constructed in the frequency domain using FFT convolution. This paper presents the SIMULINK implementation of a frequency domain channel simulator for OFDM based physical (PHY) layer of Broadband wireless access (BWA) systems. The simulator was subsequently used to study the performance of rate 1/2 coded OFDM systems employing QPSK and 16-QAM signal constellations. Long preamble aided Least Square (LS) channel estimation with low pass interpolation for even numbered data carriers has been used to equalize the effects of the channel. Three sets of representative measured channel profiles in the 2.5 GHz band have been used to study the effect of frequency selective fading on the bit error rate (BER) performance. It was found that the performance of BWA systems over a frequency selective channel mainly depended upon the frequency domain fading. Small channel variations in time did not impact the BER.

articleTitle: Microstrip antenna with shaped folded slots for multi-band applications
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: A new multi-band microstrip patch antenna element with three folded shaped slots and two coaxial feeds is presented. The designed antenna covers frequency bands ranging from GPS (1.575 GHz) to WLAN, 5.8 GHz and new DSRC, 5.9 GHz. The antenna design has been optimized to provide desired performance in GPS (1.575) GHZ, GPRS (1.85 GHz), WLAN (2.4 GHz), WLAN (5.8 GHz), and DSRC (5.9 GHz). The antenna also performs well at WiMAX band (3.5GHz). A prototype antenna has been fabricated and tested. Excellent agreement between numerical simulations and experimental results has been obtained.

articleTitle: Microstrip rhomboidal structures. numerical modelling and applications
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper some microstrip rhomboidal resonant cavities are studied. Experimental results which confirm theoretical assumtions are presented. Also, numerical modelling results basic on the Finite Element Method are presented. Two interesting applications are suggested: selective power divider and combiner.

articleTitle: Circular polarisation design of a triple fed equilateral-triangular microstrip antenna using fdtd
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: A design of triple-feed equilateral-triangular microstrip antenna for circular polarization (CP) is proposed. In this design, by feeding the patch through three points and applying proper phase differences between the feeds, CP with axial ratio close to 1 can be achieved. Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method has been applied to analyze this microstrip-fed antenna. The return loss, input impedance, far field pattern, and axial ratio are calculated and compared with the same results which are derived by HP-HFSS software.

articleTitle: Development of a passenger aircraft electromagnetic model for electromagnetic interference analysis
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Recent years have witnessed an incisive push to allow the use of wireless networks inside passenger aircraft. Because wireless devices are not subject to the same rigorous electromagnetic (EM) standards that are required for the certification of aircraft systems, the potential for electromagnetic interference (EMI) exists. Experimental determination of the response of a wide variety of aircraft types and avionics installations to interference from onboard portable electronic devices is particularly difficult and very costly. Electromagnetic modeling allows for a much more focused, timely, and repeatable evaluation than is possible with only measured data.

articleTitle: Estimating spatial correlations of the channel elements of a multiple input multiple output system based on outdoor to indoor channel measurements
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: At high SNR, strong correlations in the elements of the MIMO channel can lead to a decrease in channel capacity. In this paper we propose a new methodology to estimate these spatial correlations based on the analysis of the most significant eigenvalues of transmit and receive covariance matrices of the MIMO channel. Our study is based on measurements performed in a university campus with the following characteristics: (4 × 4) MIMO single user channels with non line of sight, outdoor to indoor and wideband for fixed wireless applications. These type of scenarios are of interest because they can be used to deploy high speed wireless internet applications.

articleTitle: Gap-loaded microstrip square ring for antenna miniaturization
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Gap-loaded microstrip square-ring antenna is investigated in this paper. Because of the gap loading, the square-ring antenna resonates at a much lower frequency than that of the unloaded case, which gives a miniaturized narrowband antenna. A detail parametric study is carried out to understand the nature of the loaded mode caused by the gap loading. An experimental prototype is fabricated and its performance is compared with simulations, confirming the computed results.

articleTitle: A wideband high-gain microstrip patch antenna with high-impedance electromagnetic band-gap ground plane
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The concept of high-impedance electromagnetic band-gap (HI-EBG) structures has been introduced in [1]. Several applications of these structures in antenna design and performance enhancement have been reported in [2]. Recently, more attention has been paid to high impedance surfaces (HISs) and their applications in the light of artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) concept [3].

articleTitle: An ultra-wide-band dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: In this paper, the broadband concept in stacked patch antennas is applied to designing broadband rectangular dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) with a small patch feed. Unlike the previous multi-segment DRA designs that have a DRA of a lower permittivity above one or more thin segments of higher permittivity, the top DR in this antenna has a higher permittivity than the lower segment. Theoretical and experimental results exhibit good agreement.

articleTitle: Efficient calculation of shielding effectiveness for rectangular enclosures with small apertures
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: A modeling technique is presented to efficiently evaluate field penetration through small apertures within a metallic cubic enclosure. The technique utilizes the moment method solution to calculate current distribution on enclosure surface area and the modal expansion technique to find field distribution over the slot aperture. In this way, one can obtain the equivalent magnetic current along the aperture from which field distributions inside the enclosure can be computed using the cavity Green's function. Simulation results are presented to examine the accuracy and other virtues of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Time-domain MoM for calculation of EM characteristics of a cellular phone handset
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The effect of cellular phone handset dimensions on radiation patterns, impedance and resonance frequency is investigated. The handset body is modeled by an appropriate three-dimensional wire-grid structure with a 2/4 monopole antenna as its radiating source. The governing electric field integral equation (EFIE) is solved in the time domain, using the method of moments (MoM). The validity of the model is demonstrated by comparing the wide-band results of the antenna input impedance with those available in the literature. It is shown that the size of a regular handset dimensions has little effect on the antenna radiation pattern and impedance.

articleTitle: A new multi-frequency reconstruction algorithm for 2-D dielectric objects buried in multilayer media using complex images green's function
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Dielectric object recognition in multilayer media has a wide range of applications in Archeology, Geophysics and mine exploration. Due to the importance of these problems, a number of different inversion algorithms have been developed for inverse scattering of buried dielectric objects [1]. In most of these algorithms measurements are carried out in a single frequency which suffers from under-estimating the permittivity profile of the buried object due to the lack of sufficient information at the measuring points.

articleTitle: Path loss model for ultra wideband signal propagation
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Ultra wideband (UWB) systems facilitate high data rates over short distances. Path loss is considered to be a fundamental parameter in channel modeling, since it plays a key role in link budget analysis. Also, path loss determines the robustness against interference and noise, which in turn influences the bit error rate behavior. Narrowband path loss models are not applicable to the path loss calculation of UWB systems. UWB transmissions occupy bandwidths of up to 7.5 GHz in the radio spectrum between 3.1 GHz and 10.6 GHz. The path loss frequency dependence cannot be ignored within such a wide band. In addition, the distance between the transmitter and receiver is assumed to be considerably less than that of traditional wireless systems. An indoor operating scenario with a range of up to 10 meters is often considered. Hence, the approximations held in a large scale are invalid and it is often required that path loss and signal degradation are handled in some scale at same time. Unprecedented wide bandwidths and short ranges require a novel approach towards the link budget calculation and channel modeling. The two-ray model is utilized extensively since it offers a simple tutorial and can produce representations of most of the behavior from practical channels. In this paper, a rigorous formulation of a two-ray link is considered and evaluated as a function of both frequency and distance, where all the assumptions adopted for deriving the traditional narrowband plane ground model are no longer valid. Considering the specific UWB application, the analysis is carried out over distance of up to 10 meters and in the operational frequency band of 3 GHz to 10 GHz. From this study, both the one- and two-slope analytical path loss models for short range, two-ray links with wide operational bandwidths are derived, which are considered to be good approximations for line-of-sight (LOS) UWB links operating in a relatively clutter-free environment. On the basis of this, the frequency and distance characteristics of the path loss are discussed, and some meaningful conclusions for UWB system analysis and design are drawn.

articleTitle: Compact CMOS VCO using a transistor for frequency control
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: A compact CMOS voltage-controlled relaxation oscillator circuit is presented in this paper. The frequency control is fulfilled by using a single MOSFET to control the charging and discharging currents of a timing capacitor. This paper investigates and demonstrates the proposed control mechanism. The proposed VCO was fabricated using 0.18 μm CMOS technology and the fabricated VCO has a compact core size of only 80μm × 200μm, or 0.016mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. A linear tuning range from 650 MHz to 840 MHz, or a 28% range was achieved by the single MOSFET's control from a 1.8V DC supply voltage. The output power was −14.5 dBm with only ±1 dB variation in this tuning range. The corresponding power consumption was measured to be 5.4mW. Moreover, the VCO free-running frequency can be increased beyond 1.1 GHz by using higher DC supply.

articleTitle: A DSP based retrodirective array for duplex digital communications at 2.4 GHz
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Retrodirective arrays are unique phased array systems that are capable of providing power gain in the direction of a received source with no prior knowledge of the source's location. When compared to fully adaptive arrays that adjust their beam patterns to the signal environment based on the received spatial signature, retrodirective arrays have small computational burdens for antenna pattern adaptation. Traditionally, retrodirective arrays have been designed around analog methods such as doubled local oscillator phase conjugation and heterodyning for use in line of sight non-fading channels. In this paper, we present a novel implementation of a retrodirective array for duplex digital communications and show that the retrodirective array can enhance system performance in a multipath environment. Measurements of the retrodirective array using flexible uplink and downlink modulation schemes are presented. They prove experimentally that the designed system is capable of tracking a signal source accurately under duplex communications conditions.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized broadband antenna with L-shaped probe and wide slot
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Several circularly polarized broadband antennas and polarizers have been investigated[1]-[4] to handle large volume of information for mainly satellite communications and radars. In view of these applications, these require broadband characteristics in both input impedance matching and radiation characteristics like axial ratio(AR) and gain.

articleTitle: A design optimization framework for multi-band body-of-revolution antenna feeds — Application to a prime-focus dual-band coaxial feed
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: The development of software radios has brought about a need for multi-band antenna feeds for use in the radio-frequency front-ends of satellite ground terminals. To provide the tools necessary for the design of such feeds, we have developed the Framework for Antenna Design and Optimization (FADO), a computer-based antenna design optimization framework based on the combination of custom-designed synthesis and analysis software, a commercial body-of-revolution electromagnetics simulation tool (AKBOR2, by Kishk Consulting), a high-frequency reflector modelling tool (Grasp, by TICRA), and a global optimizer (glbfast, part of the Tomlaboptimization suite). The capabilities of this new design tool are demonstrated through the design of a compact dual-band Ku/X coaxial antenna feed for a 4.6-m single-reflector antenna Using FADO, a compact dual-band feed was designed and optimized by combining a dielectric-filled circular waveguide ending in a tapered dielectric rod, which launches the Ku-band waves, and a coaxial aperture launching the X-band waves. Proper reflector illumination was achieved in both frequency bands. This resulted in aperture efficiencies above 66% at X band and 62% at Ku band, secondary-beam cross-polarization levels of −57 dB at X band and −37 dB at Ku band, and sidelobe levels lower than the maximum sidelobe envelope as per IntelSat's standard. A ring-based filter integrated in the coaxial channel is shown to improve coaxial rejection of the Ku-band signal while providing adequate impedance matching capability for the X-band signal. A Ku-band isolation better than 19.4 dB and an X-band input match better than −17 dB are achieved. As part of a separate optimization, two air-gap rings were integrated within the dielectric-filled circular waveguide, which allowed for an improvement of the Ku-band input match from −10.5 dB to −15.2 dB.

articleTitle: Wireless communication systems in healthcare: Development of a new multi-source electromagnetic-compatibility criterion
publicationTitle: 2006 12th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and Canadian Radio Sciences Conference
abstract: Future healthcare informatics needs at the point of care will require the usage of multiple radio-frequency (RF) sources near medical devices. Current electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) criteria in hospitals recommend that a minimum separation be maintained between a single RF source and a medical device, but they say nothing about multiple RF sources, and are therefore inadequate when multiple sources are present. This paper describes a new EMC separation criterion specifying a minimum separation distance when N RF sources operate in an indoor-propagation scenario. The new separation criterion is based on the direct field of N nearby sources, which increases the separation distance by √N, and the indirect or reverberant field of these sources, which depends on the combined power of all sources in the room and the room absorption. Simulations are shown to illustrate the usefulness and validity of the new criterion.

articleTitle: Maxwell's legacy

abstract: Working with RF has been a passion of mine ever since I learned how to grab a soldering iron by the right (EM) has held my attention for the last two decades.
